answer: An agent economy can keep fake identities scarce by making entry pass through a sponsor: a newcomer joins only when an established agent stakes part of its own standing on them, and each sponsor may vouch for just one newcomer per epoch. A fake that misbehaves burns its sponsor's stake, so honest agents guard their summit slot carefully. The cost of a fake army grows with every shale identity an attacker wants, since each needs a separate sponsor that no parallel compute can create. The pulse of new entry stays tied to the community's growth, not to how many keys an attacker can generate.
